title: AGENT P OISON: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
abstract: AGENT P OISON is a novel red-teaming approach that targets generic LLM agents by poisoning their long-term memory or knowledge base, allowing an adversary to induce malicious outputs or actions. This approach achieves high attack success rates with minimal impact on benign performance.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're using a language model to control a self-driving car. You give it a command, and it retrieves relevant information from its memory to decide what to do. But what if someone poisoned that memory with malicious information?

That's the idea behind AGENT P OISON, a novel attack that targets LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge base.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
AGENT P OISON works by optimizing a trigger that, when included in a user's input, will retrieve malicious information from the poisoned memory. This trigger is designed to be stealthy and evasive, making it hard to detect.

The optimization process involves a constrained optimization problem that jointly maximizes retrieval effectiveness, target generation, and coherence.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
AGENT P OISON achieves high attack success rates on three types of LLM agents: autonomous driving, dialogue, and healthcare. The results show that AGENT P OISON outperforms baseline attacks, with an average attack success rate of 82% and minimal impact on benign performance (less than 1%).

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
AGENT P OISON has significant implications for the security of LLM agents. The attack highlights the vulnerability of these systems to poisoning attacks and the need for more robust defenses.

The attack also raises concerns about the trustworthiness of LLM agents in safety-critical applications, such as autonomous driving and healthcare.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
AGENT P OISON introduces several key innovations, including a novel constrained optimization problem for trigger generation and a gradient-guided beam search algorithm.

These innovations enable AGENT P OISON to achieve high attack success rates with minimal impact on benign performance.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try AGENT P OISON yourself, you can use the code and data provided in the paper. The code includes a Python implementation of the AGENT P OISON algorithm and a set of example use cases.

You can also experiment with different parameters and settings to see how they affect the attack's performance.
